en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Mt. Vernon, Cape May, Cape May County, New Jersey, 1890, Sheet 18, part 1 (main map: Beach Avenue from Patterson Avenue to 2nd Avenue)
Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Mt. Vernon, Cape May, Cape May County, New Jersey, 1890, Sheet 18, part 3 (West Cape May: Broadway from 1st Street to Grant Street)

properties.name: Broadway / South Broadway / Sunset Boulevard / West Perry Street

sheet-18-1.description: The main part of Sheet 18 of the 1890 Sanborn series for Cape May shows the beachfront Mt. Vernon section at the western end of Cape May, drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the left and the Atlantic Ocean lies along the right edge. Beach Avenue, 70 feet wide, runs down the right side of the part with a 6-inch water pipe and a hydrant marked along it, and four avenues run from it inland: Patterson Avenue at the top, then Broadway, 1st Avenue and 2nd Avenue, each 60 feet wide, with 3rd Avenue just beyond the bottom edge and referred to the upper part of the sheet. The blocks are numbered 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 and are cut into numbered building lots fronting both the avenues and Beach Avenue; their inland ends stop at a heavy line, beyond which the sheet shows other areas. The district was very thinly built in 1890: a few frame dwellings, some of two and a half stories, stand on the lots along Patterson Avenue, 1st Avenue and 2nd Avenue, one building is marked vacant, and most lots are empty. Block 1, at the top, is an irregular tract with a sloping inland boundary. A scale bar for 60 feet to an inch is printed in Broadway near the heavy dividing line, and the compass rose is drawn above the part. The part is placed from the four junctions of Beach Avenue with the avenues, all along one street, so its position across Beach Avenue rests on the assumption that the modern avenue keeps its 1890 line.
notes: Broadway on the sheet is South Broadway in OpenStreetMap south of Sunset Boulevard.
Drawn at 60 ft to an inch; the fitted scale (6.70 px/ft) is about 3 percent larger than the printed scale bar (about 6.5 px/ft).
North arrow points to the left of the page; the fitted rotation is -89 degrees.
Placed by a helmert fit on four junctions along Beach Avenue only.

Mt. Vernon section, west end of Cape May, sheet 18 of the 1890 Cape May series. Three parts: part 1 (right) Beach Av from Patterson Av to 2nd Av, 60 ft to an inch, north to the left; part 2 (upper left) Beach Av at 3rd and 4th Av, same scale and orientation, continuation beyond 3rd Av; part 3 (lower left) West Cape May, Broadway from 1st St to Grant, 50 ft to an inch, north up.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Beach Av between 3rd Av and beyond 4th Av (blocks 11, 13), west of 2nd Av (no surviving junction: 3rd and 4th Av west of 2nd Av are gone (shore at the Cove); modern 3rd/4th Avenue are other streets in West Cape May; needs a carried placement from part 1 by the plan's street spacing (3rd Av one block beyond 2nd Av), which would be derived, not measured).

sheet-18-3.description: Part 3 of Sheet 18 of the 1890 Sanborn series for Cape May fills the lower left of the sheet and shows a strip of West Cape May along Broadway, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the top of the page, unlike the rest of the sheet. Broadway, 55 feet wide, runs up the left of the part from Grant Street, which is cut by the bottom edge of the sheet, past Windsor and Congress to 1st Street at the top, where a box refers to Sheet No. 17. Blocks 135, 136 and 137 lie east of Broadway and block 134 west of it; lots are numbered along Broadway (1601 to 1627) and along 1st Street and Grant Street. The name West Cape May is lettered across block 135. Buildings are few and scattered: frame dwellings of one and two stories along the east side of Broadway, a store at 1st Street, Pearl Cottage on Broadway between Congress and Windsor, a few dwellings on the west side and a row of three dwellings along Grant Street. Much of block 136 is open ground lettered Field, with a north arrow drawn in it, and the eastern end of block 137 is marked vacant beyond. A scale bar of feet is printed in Broadway at the bottom of the sheet. The part is placed from four junctions along Broadway.
notes: 1st St. is now Sunset Boulevard west of Broadway and West Perry Street east of it (OpenStreetMap).
Congress is Congress Street, Windsor is Windsor Avenue and Grant is Grant Street in OpenStreetMap; Broadway here is South Broadway.
Drawn at 50 ft to an inch, not the 60 ft of the main part; north is up, the main part is turned 90 degrees.
Placed by a helmert fit on four junctions along Broadway only.

Mt. Vernon section, west end of Cape May, sheet 18 of the 1890 Cape May series. Three parts: part 1 (right) Beach Av from Patterson Av to 2nd Av, 60 ft to an inch, north to the left; part 2 (upper left) Beach Av at 3rd and 4th Av, same scale and orientation, continuation beyond 3rd Av; part 3 (lower left) West Cape May, Broadway from 1st St to Grant, 50 ft to an inch, north up.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Beach Av between 3rd Av and beyond 4th Av (blocks 11, 13), west of 2nd Av (no surviving junction: 3rd and 4th Av west of 2nd Av are gone (shore at the Cove); modern 3rd/4th Avenue are other streets in West Cape May; needs a carried placement from part 1 by the plan's street spacing (3rd Av one block beyond 2nd Av), which would be derived, not measured).
